facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation

presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation

concepts.why: Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive support this diagnosis.
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest chronic rhinosinusitis.
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex and vision loss in the right eye support this diagnosis.
Opacification of the sphenoid sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest sphenoid sinusitis.
Opacification of the ethmoid sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest ethmoid sinusitis.
Opacification of the maxillary sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest maxillary sinusitis.
Opacification of the frontal sinus and positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus suggest frontal sinusitis.
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19 and subsequent development of rhinosinusitis symptoms suggest post-COVID-19 rhinosinusitis.
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation suggest invasive fungal sinusitis.
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation into the apex and vision loss in the right eye support this diagnosis.

rationales.F03: Vision loss in one eye is a key feature of C03
rationales.F04: Recent COVID-19 diagnosis could be related to C08
rationales.F05: Severe vision loss is consistent with C03
rationales.F07: Opacification of all sinuses on the right is consistent with C02, C04, C05, C06, and C07
rationales.F08: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone is a key feature of C03
rationales.F09: Elevated Serum IgG4 is a key feature of C01
rationales.F10: Positive sinus cultures could be related to C02, C04, C05, C06, C07, C08, or C09
rationales.F11: Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells is a key feature of C01

frontier_selector.rationale: Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG4-positive plasma cells support IgG4-related disease, which also explains the orbital apex syndrome findings
